status: Isolated guest prototype; NOT installed or selected by native module registration.
moduleContract: Exactly8 pinned ESM exports. Default is an ordinary object whose initial method references match the named exports; encode===stringify and decode===parse. Reassigning a default property does not rewrite named bindings, while parser/stringifier use mutable default escape/unescape hooks as pinned Node does. Future selected literal CommonJS lowering may return default; runtime require and syncBuiltinESMExports remain excluded.

node:querystring.callablePolicy: Nonstring unescapeBuffer overloads throw TypeError ERR_SM_NODE_UNSUPPORTED with operation on call or construction. Resource caps throw RangeError ERR_SM_NODE_LIMIT. No blank objects, universal Proxy or silent failure substitutes for declared bindings.
node:querystring.parseContract: Null-prototype output; duplicate key aggregation; safe own __proto__ fields; custom separators/equal delimiters; Node1000 default segment limit; positive integer maxKeys decrement and exact pinned fractional/nonpositive/NaN/Infinity behavior within profile hard caps. Empty segments count toward Node maxKeys. Custom decoder callbacks receive plus as %20 and exceptions fall back through mutable default.unescape. Callback return values are not restricted to strings, following pinned Node behavior.
node:querystring.codecContract: Captured native URI encoding/decoding fast paths. On malformed UTF16, escape emulates Node22 legacy surrogate pairing and terminal URIError ERR_INVALID_URI. Malformed percent fallback scans UTF16 code units into bytes modulo256 then decodes nonfatal UTF8 preserving BOM through existing guest Buffer.toString. No URLSearchParams or TextEncoder substitution.
deviations: Profile hard caps are additional to Node maxKeys and cannot be disabled by maxKeys0, negative, fractional, NaN or Infinity. Failed caps may occur after earlier callback/getter effects; no rollback is promised.

Nonstring unescapeBuffer is explicitly deferred, including fallback after a failing nonstring unescape coercion. Native successful unescape scalar/object coercions remain supported within output input-size bound.

unescapeBuffer allocates using supported captured Buffer.alloc rather than deferred allocUnsafe. Every returned byte is initialized; Buffer pooling/uninitialized unused backing semantics are not claimed.
Buffer allocation, shared slice views, Uint8Array brand and UTF8 replacement follow the bounded core Buffer profile. This does not expand its encodings, limits or APIs.

Native intrinsic and Buffer allocation/slice references are captured. Application callbacks and mutable default hooks execute with Node's inspected invocation order; arbitrary engine-specific stack/error formatting is not claimed.
Proxy-backed arrays with noninteger/nonfinite reported lengths are deferred. Exact out-of-memory behavior and performance/size comparison remain unmeasured.
